description: Sodium-water safety demo cell: an FBRK-walled pit holding a WATR pool with an NA charge suspended above it on a shelf gap, ready to drop.
name: sodium_fire_demo
why: Sodium metal (melts 98 C) reacts violently with water: NA+WATR/DSTW releases ~600 K of heat and H2 gas that then ignites -- a real and historically documented hazard at sodium-cooled reactor sites. This is a HAZARD DEMO, not a toy: the FBRK containment (acid/heat resistant, a decent insulator) keeps the fire and blast local. The NA block sits on a dry shelf above the pool at rest; unpausing lets gravity drop it in. Never build this with a conductive (METL) enclosure, and never site it near stored fuel or logic.
